newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ says year profit to be materially lower.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ says year profit to be materially lower.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd said on Wednesday it expects its full year profit in 1996/97 will be materially below the previous year's NZ$225.2 million.
Air NZ said that, as stated when it undertook a cash issue in late 1996, it intended to maintain the current annual dividend rate at 20 cents per share on the expanded share capital.

It said 51.2 percent of revenue for the 1997 interim period was generated offshore and it was estimated that currency movements accounted for a revenue reduction of about $50 million, countered somewhat by cost savings on offshore expenditure.
Earlier, Air NZ said net profit in the six months to December 31 fell 43 percent to $76.7 million.
The seasonal increase in oil prices that traditionally occurs during the northern hemisphere winter emerged earlier than had been the custom, and prevailed for longer than expected.

The total fuel cost for the six months was $178.7 million, a 17.9 percent increase over the comparative period notwithstanding an increase of only 2.2 percent in aircraft capacity flown and the effects of a stronger New Zealand dollar.

"These influences have posed substantial challenges for the company and for the New Zealand tourism industry at large, by making New Zealand more expensive to visit and therefore less attractive vis-a-vis competing international destinations."
